preamble: In Jèrriais, the Norman language of Jersey, /r/ between vowels and word-finally after a vowel developed into the voiced dental fricative [ð], written 'th'. The change happened after the 16th century: Sercquiais, brought to Sark by Jersey settlers, does not have it, and the eastern dialects of Jersey also lack it. No comparable regular r > ð change has been confirmed in another language, so the shift is rare.
sources: Wikipedia contributors. Jèrriais: Phonology, Dental fricative. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A8rriais
